title: Multi-AZ Resilience, Deployments & Recovery Controls
summary: Static stability, zonal shift, safe deployments and fault injection for highly available workloads.
tldr: Spread every tier across **at least two AZs**: Auto Scaling groups, load balancer subnets, NAT gateways (one per AZ), Lambda VPC subnets, databases and file systems.
**Static stability**: pre-provision enough capacity that losing one AZ needs no new launches (e.g. ~150% of peak across 3 AZs, so any 2 AZs carry full load).
Move traffic away from an impaired AZ with **ARC zonal shift / zonal autoshift**; move it between Regions with **ARC routing controls** or Global Accelerator **traffic dials**.
Deploy safely with **immutable** releases (new AMI + instance refresh), **blue/green**, and the ECS **deployment circuit breaker**; test it with **AWS Fault Injection Service**.

keyFacts.text: A single-instance legacy app across AZs: an Auto Scaling group with capacity 1 spanning several AZs relaunches it anywhere after a failure.
**Simplified automatic recovery** brings an instance back on new hardware with the same ID, private IP, Elastic IP and EBS data, which suits license-bound servers.
Turn on ELB health checks for the Auto Scaling group, with a grace period, so instances that pass EC2 status checks but fail the app are replaced.
Turn on **cross-zone load balancing** (off by default on NLB) when target counts per AZ are uneven, so traffic spreads across all targets.
**Service Quotas** are per Region and account. A standby Region must have quotas raised to production size before failover.

traps: Scaling policies that launch instances *during* an AZ event aren't static stability. Capacity must already be running.
One NAT gateway or one Lambda subnet in a single AZ is a hidden single point of failure.
EFS **One Zone** and FSx **Single-AZ** don't survive an AZ failure. Pick Regional EFS or Multi-AZ FSx.
EBS volumes and Multi-Attach are tied to one AZ. They can't share data across AZs.
Rolling updates with min 100% / max 200% still mix old and new versions. Use blue/green when traffic must switch all at once.
An Auto Scaling replacement is a *new* instance with a new ID and IP. When the license is bound to the instance, use EC2 automatic recovery instead.
